title.narrative: Output 3.2. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative: The Government of Liberia, in collaboration with social partners and other relevant stakeholders, operationalized a strategy for employment in rural areas. This strategy promotes social cohesion and enhances sustainable and inclusive economic and human development by fostering rural employment opportunities and establishing cooperative businesses for youth, women and other vulnerable groups. The operationalization of the employment strategy led to the following results. A total of 287 persons (of whom 167 were women) predominantly vulnerable community members, benefited from capacity building actions. Of this number, 264 (females: 158 and males: 106) benefited from the Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB)programme which seeks to provide more and better employment. The remaining 23 (9 women and 14 men) were beneficiaries of the Cooperative Development and Governance programme for sustainable and inclusive economic and human development in Lofa, Bong, and Nimba Counties. The ILO organized and facilitated a series of capacity building actions in Lofa, Bong and Nimba Counties. The ILO provided support through a joint project implemented with FAO, UNDP, UN Women and WFP funded by the UN Human Security Trust Fund. The project aims to address the complex multi-sectorial and interconnected challenges of human insecurities particularly food, social, and economic issues for the most vulnerable and neglected populations of the North-Central region of Liberia at the community level. Between November 2022 and June 2023, the ILO, in collaboration with the Ministries of Labour, Internal Affairs, Finance and Development Planning and other key stakeholders facilitated a series of step-down trainings on Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB). Through this project, the ILO provided them with start-up capital to invest in their developed business plans. In August 2023, the ILO supported a training of trainers workshop in cooperative development and governance, using Start Coop and My.Coop tools. The workshop took place in Gbarnga, Bong County. The ILO also recruited all the consultants who facilitated these capacity building workshops.
